walkPatron.about: Who pays for the Walk in secret, by what the Walk is for. A grieving dowager pays for a penance, never for a reform; a factor who wants the road free of tolls pays for a reform; a Warden's cousin, who wants the Bench's seat for a friend, pays for any.

walkLeader.about: Who leads, by what the Walk is for.

walkBound.about: What would move the bailiff, by who holds him. A bailiff in a patron's debt is moved by the proof of it; any other is moved by his own kin on the road, or by the book of his office.

remembrance: that the Keepers of the Road will come again to the road they kept, the day every mile of it has been spoken aloud by a living mouth
penance: that the road carried our dead away when the Empire ended, and must be walked back, mile by mile, until they are home
reform: that the road belongs to whoever walks it, and that a man who sets a toll on a mile he did not lay has stolen it

remembrance: Keep it, keep it, keep it again
penance: Bring them home, bring them home
reform: No toll, no toll, no toll on the road

scrivener: a village scrivener who read the stones before anyone, and was laughed at, and went on reading
soldier: a soldier turned off without his pay, who counted the road's miles on the way home and has not stopped counting
widow: a widow who buried a husband and two sons from the road in one bad year, and began walking it to find where they went
novice: a novice who left her house at night with her sandals in her hand, because a mile of the road had spoken to her
drover: a drover whose hip was stove in by a cart on the old road, and who has walked on it ever since

cousin: Sir Aldric Vane, the Warden's cousin
Sir Gervase Holt, the Warden's cousin
factor: the factor Osbert Wynne, of the wool-house
the factor Hesper Calloway, of the salt-house

dowager: that her son's name be said at the Station, which the church will not allow him, he having died on the road unshriven
cousin: a crowd that will frighten the Hundred into asking a better man to sit in the bailiff's chair, and the better man is a friend of his
factor: a road without a toll, and a Hundred without a bailiff to take one
